title: Huawei Defies US Sanctions With Ascend 960 & Optical SuperPoD!
summary: Huawei moved forward the launch of its Ascend 960DT and 960PR AI processors to 2027 while unveiling its Atlas 960E SuperPoD architecture. The design uses proprietary UnifiedBus interconnects and near-packaged optics to tie together 4,096 processors without relying on advanced Western lithography.
raw_text: If you thought export bans would stop China's semiconductor ambitions, think again. Huawei just pulled forward their entire Ascend 960 AI silicon roadmap, and their new system architecture is an engineering masterclass. Because they are blocked from buying cutting-edge EUV lithography machines and foreign HBM, Huawei is compensating with pure interconnect genius. They unveiled the Atlas 960E SuperPoD, linking 4,096 processors into an integrated computing monster delivering 16 exaflops of FP4 throughput. Here's the wild part: they integrated Hi-ONE near-packaged optics directly onto the processor packages, completely eliminating 48,000 optical transceivers and slashing power consumption by 550 kilowatts. By splitting compute into specialized 960DT decode chips and 960PR prefill chips, they are achieving frontier performance despite massive geopolitical sanctions. It is a brilliant hardware workaround that proves system-level packaging might matter just as much as raw transistor shrink!

title: Carl Pei Spins Off CMF as Independent Indian Brand Under MPSE!
summary: Nothing CEO Carl Pei announced the corporate spin-off of sub-brand CMF into an independent, majority Indian-owned hardware company. The restructuring capitalizes on India's Rs. 62,500 crore MPSE manufacturing subsidy program to localize design and component sourcing.
raw_text: Carl Pei is pulling off one of the smartest supply chain maneuvers in modern consumer tech! He just announced that Nothing's sub-brand, CMF, is officially spinning off into a completely independent, majority Indian-owned hardware company. London-based Nothing is retaining a minority stake, but CMF will now run its own R&D, supply chain, and product design directly out of India. Why pull this move? Because of India's massive Rs. 62,500 crore MPSE incentive scheme. While nearly all phones sold in India are assembled locally, this new program rewards brands that shift high-value component engineering and intellectual property onto Indian soil. By establishing CMF as an indigenous domestic player, they unlock huge state subsidies, bypass punishing import tariffs, and build a localized hardware powerhouse. It's a masterstroke in navigating global trade protectionism while aggressively courting the world's fastest-growing smartphone consumer base!

title: Intel in High-Stakes Negotiations With SK Hynix for Ohio HBM Fab!

raw_text: Intel is fighting hard to turn its foundry business around, and an unexpected partnership with South Korea's memory leader might be their lifeline! SK Hynix has entered exploratory talks with Intel to manufacture cutting-edge DRAM and High-Bandwidth Memory directly inside Intel's mega-campus in New Albany, Ohio. Intel Foundry recorded a painful $2.1 billion operating deficit last quarter, and commercial wafer production at the Ohio plant has already slipped toward 2030. Bringing in SK Hynix as an anchor tenant gives Intel immediate lease revenue and offsets crushing overhead costs. For SK Hynix, building packaging lines on American soil protects their vital Nvidia HBM supply chain from Asian geopolitical friction. That said, advanced packaging is classified as protected national tech by Seoul, so regulatory clearances will be intense. If completed, this deal could finally breathe life into Intel's massive Ohio manufacturing hub!
